info:
  title: Kumori BDI Monitor listener
  version: "1.0"
  description: Boomi Integration Web Services Server listener that lists Boomi Data Integration flows (read-only).
servers:
  - url: https://boomi.kumori.ai
security:
  - listenerAuth: []
paths:
  /ws/simple/getListFlows:
    get:
      operationId: listFlows
      security:
        - listenerAuth: []
      summary: List BDI flows
      responses:
        "200":
          description: BDI Rivers API list, passed through by the Integration process
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/FlowList"

  securitySchemes:
    listenerAuth:
      type: apiKey

      name: Authorization

  schemas:
    FlowList:
      type: object
      properties:
        total_items:
          type: integer
        items:
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: "#/components/schemas/Flow"
    Flow:
      type: object
      properties:
        river_cross_id:
          type: string
        name:
          type: string
        river_type:
          type: string
        river_status:
          type: string
        last_updated_at:
          type: string
        description:
          type: string

contentValues.f539fe5f-789a-4d54-895e-afccb5f12235:
Under the hood: what one press calls

  1. Boomi Flow: a Database Load step reads the type BDI Flow List:items through Flow's OpenAPI connector, Kumori BDI Listener, which sends GET https://boomi.kumori.ai/ws/simple/getListFlows with a signed-in login.
  2. Cloudflare and our gateway: Cloudflare passes the call to our Google Cloud VM, where the gateway forwards only Boomi listener paths to the runtime.
  3. Boomi Integration: the Web Services Server listener [WSS] BDI List Pipelines starts the process [LISTENER] BDI List Pipelines, which calls the subprocess [SUB] BDI List Pipelines.
  4. Boomi Integration to Data Integration: the subprocess's REST step, BDI Rivers API: List Pipelines, calls GET https://api.rivery.io/v1/accounts/{account}/environments/{environment}/rivers with a token held in an environment extension, never in a component.
  5. Boomi Data Integration answers with the pipeline list; it travels back the same way into the table, and an operator step stamps the time.

The Boomi runtime, built the way we build for clients

The Boomi Integration runtime behind this app is ours, on Google Cloud, set up the way we recommend to customers:

  • Hardened host: Boomi's official runtime container on Google's Container-Optimized OS, with its data on a managed Docker volume.
  • Nothing open to the internet but the front door: the cloud firewall admits only Cloudflare's network, and the server answers only the Boomi listener paths; every other path returns not-found.
  • Encrypted all the way: TLS from your browser to Cloudflare and again from Cloudflare to the server, with Cloudflare's origin certificate.
  • Every call signs in: the listener requires a login, and admin access to the machine is through Google's Identity-Aware Proxy only, never an open SSH port.
  • No secrets in code: every token lives in Google Secret Manager, each readable only by the one service that needs it, and rotated by script.

contentValues.543479be-50e6-4503-8742-c4db109fb908:
Live demo · built in Boomi Flow

Ask Boomi for our pipelines, right now

Kumori runs all three parts of Boomi's platform together: Boomi Data Integration moves our data, Boomi Integration runs the logic on our own Google Cloud runtime, and this app, built in Boomi Flow, puts a face on it. One press sends a real request through five hops and back, usually in about a second.

  1. 1Boomi FlowThis app asks our API
  2. 2CloudflareChecks the request and forwards it to Google Cloud
  3. 3Boomi Integration runtimeOur own runtime checks the login
  4. 4Integration processCalls the Boomi Data Integration API
  5. 5Boomi Data IntegrationAnswers with our pipelines

This page is a light shim over the live chain. The full version, with every detail, screenshots and results, is kumori.ai/whats-new/boomi-data-integration. Read-only: nothing runs and no credits are spent.
